children: What Happened?
A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after software stocks extended gains as the broader stock market undergoes an overhaul regarding the future of the artificial intelligence trade.

Repricing continued to unfold following the previous week’s sharp retreat in tech equities, when mounting financing hurdles weakened demand for physical artificial intelligence builders. As reported by CNBC, high-growth software stocks are looking increasingly attractive as market participants rotate money out of the semiconductor sector and into the parts of the AI trade that they believe will outperform going forward. CNBC noted that this rotation is being driven by growing investor weariness that the broader market will face a challenging environment next year due to a ballooning U.S. fiscal deficit, higher inflation, and an anticipated deceleration in the massive AI infrastructure capital expenditure cycle.

Furthermore, CNBC explained that the earlier narrative surrounding "software obsolescence"—where investors feared AI agents could replace traditional software packages—has largely receded as strong earnings expectations and new AI product partnerships revive confidence in the sector.

Ultimately, CNBC observed that this shift in sentiment has created a pronounced divergence in the market, with software sector ETFs climbing sharply in recent months while semiconductor ETFs suffer extended, historic losing streaks.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming In On monday.com (MNDY)

monday.com’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 49 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 5 days ago when the stock gained 8% on the news that software-as-a-service and broader technology equities rebounded as falling Treasury yields attracted dip-buyers back into the market following a sharp, AI-driven sell-off in previous sessions.

As reported by CNBC, major equity averages—including the tech-heavy Nasdaq—moved higher as market sentiment stabilized and capital rotated back into quality software. In the previous session, CNBC noted that shares across the artificial intelligence and broader technology space had faced heightened selling pressure, rattling investor confidence regarding near-term monetization and the heavy debt burdens funding the AI sector. However, CNBC observed that this pullback proved short-lived as dip-buyers re-entered the market, viewing the sector's valuation reset as an attractive entry point for companies with fortress balance sheets. Contributing heavily to the improved sentiment, CNBC reported that the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield—which recently hit its highest point since 2002—pulled back, providing a crucial reprieve for the market. CNBC highlighted this relationship, explaining that falling yields provide a tailwind for high-growth SaaS stocks because lower interest rates make the long-dated future cash flows of these tech companies more attractive to investors.

Ultimately, CNBC noted that this swift recovery highlights an enduring investor appetite for leading software firms, even as Wall Street remains highly sensitive to how quickly massive capital investments in artificial intelligence will translate into sustainable corporate profits.

monday.com is down 29.9% since the beginning of the year, and at $100.49 per share, it is trading 51% below its 52-week high of $205.24 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of monday.com’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $273.34.
